THE_CROSS_CHECK_THAT_SETTLED_IT: 222 against 223. THE DIFFERENCE OF EXACTLY ONE IS A CONCEPT WHOSE IDENTICAL NAME, KIND AND DESCRIPTION OCCURS IN TWO FAMILIES — so `family` is still doing work at the widened grain and dropping it would SILENTLY MERGE THAT PAIR. Two independent derivations agreeing on ~223 and disagreeing by exactly the amount ONE FIELD EXPLAINS is worth more than either number alone: A DISCREPANCY YOU CAN ACCOUNT FOR IS STRONGER EVIDENCE THAN AN AGREEMENT YOU CANNOT.
⚠️ TWO DIVERGENCES, BOTH ON `description: FIRST: these subjects' searchText is `Artifact vN | TypeName` and does NOT contain the description, so RENDERING and RETRIEVAL diverge for this population — the same shape as P0b-R2's 2,213-versus-2,347 on the property tier. SECOND, and it sharpens the first rather than merely coexisting with it: the 67 impure groups differ in EXACTLY THE FIELD THAT IS RENDERED AND NOT EMBEDDED. So the representative's choice changes WHAT THE JUDGE READS while changing NOTHING about what was RETRIEVED. Widening the key to 223 fixes the second and leaves the first untouched — the first is a forge-composition question and a NEW authorisation, and it is TQ's.
whatWasREJECTEDandWhy: Narrowing the rendering allow-list so `description` is not shown would also have satisfied the rule, at 156. REJECTED by SABLE_RIVER: the description is the RICHEST PROSE IN THE STANDARD (non-empty on 346 of 452, mean 183 characters) and THE ONLY REAL EVIDENCE THESE SUBJECTS HAVE — their searchText is an artifact-and-version prefix plus a type name. Take it away and the judge is asked to map a bare type name to a CEDS card. 'We would be buying key purity by removing the evidence, which is not a trade, it is a loss wearing a rule's clothing.'
howThisWasChecked: forges/pesc260805/test/probes/p1_optionSetKeyPurity.js, retained. It READS THE ALLOW-LIST FROM THE SHIPPED DECLARATION rather than restating it, so the check and the thing checked cannot drift apart; and it REFUSES TO RUN AT ALL if the declaration names a field it does not read, because A PURITY CHECK OVER A SUBSET OF THE ALLOW-LIST WOULD REPORT PURITY IT NEVER MEASURED — a green answer to a smaller question than the one asked.
